pose: unchanged target glTF bind pose in metres, Y up; anatomical forward is -Z; anatomical left is -X

method.topology: Weld exported vertices by exact POSITION, find singly used edges and trace closed boundaries in sorted-index order. Boot has two 22-point cuff loops. Both 12-point lower trousers boundaries end below their corresponding ankle. Refer to signed triangle indices in the pinned GLBs.
method.rayOrigin: For each boot direction use the mean XZ of its 22-point cuff. At the rim use that vertex Y; repeat the same XZ unit rays at the preexisting shaft midpoint and ankle heights in fit-report.json. For trouser hems use their own 12-point ring center and each hem vertex Y.
method.directions: atan2(ipsilateral X, -Z) degrees; zero forward, +90 lateral, -90 medial and +/-180 heelward. i is the zero-based position in the welded traced loop, not a bone ID. rayXYZ and the origin define the raw ray.
method.intersections: Two-sided Moller-Trumbore on source mesh triangles at the specified Y; retain positive ray distances, merge hits within 0.000001 m. Use the first skin/trousers intersection only if the count is odd from the same-sided origin. Record all boot hits. For a ray exactly through a real cuff vertex, also include its known radius even if edge/numerical coincidence drops that intersection. The hull of those radii is a radial span of the visible geometry, not the material thickness normal to a sheet.
method.pointRule: allowableRadialDeltaMM = [skinRadius - bootRadius, pantsRadius - bootRadius] for the boundary point or outermost boot surface. A positive lower bound needs an outward move; a negative upper bound needs an inward move.
method.spanRule: For inner/outer observed boot radii [I,O] use allowableSpanDeltaMM = [skinRadius-I, pantsRadius-O]. An interval of nonnegative width allows the whole sampled span to translate radially between the two fixed surfaces. max(lower) > min(upper) excludes a common radial offset. Half the minimum individual window is the largest equal two-sided radial reserve in these independent samples, not a production tolerance.
method.groundReference: Split the planted shoe and flat control at the ankle and ball by projecting onto the horizontal ankle-to-ball axis. Record regional minimum vertex Y. This is neutral geometry, not proof of active heel contact.
method.regionProbe: Re-run surfaces.crossings on all boot triangles classified by min/max Y around each target ankle. Pair counts reproduce the archived full crossing totals. Knee clearance is geometric height to the reference joint.

decision.neutralCuff: Every sampled cuff span has a positive radial placement window. For a visible upper shaft defect, start with the existing boot-specific fit, retaining the source cuff topology and working against both signed bounds. This one pose and finite sample do not guarantee a continuous or animated fit.
decision.hem: Seven of twelve actual hem directions per side pass inside the boot outer surface; the others lie outside. If the intended visible order is pants outside boot and that defect is confirmed below the ankle, address the specific trousers hem fit there. If pants are intentionally tucked inside the boot, review the opposite order. The complete leg has no single established layer order in this unmodified fixture.
decision.frozenGeometry: Keep tread, original vamp and reference knee/bone axes fixed for any upper-cuff-only trial. The knee is over 316 mm above the boot; preserving the existing skin and sole keeps the original control meaningful. Nonzero intersections already entirely below the ankle mean changing the cuff cannot fix the whole foot. Trouser changes alone also cannot clear bare-foot intersections.
decision.footContact: The forefoot regional minimum is shared, but the boot heel region is about 6.14 mm higher than the flat control. Review gait/contact separately if it appears in moving footage, before considering changes to the footbed.
decision.limits: Intervals are radial in neutral pose, not Euclidean normal clearances, safe offsets, live visibility or evidence of failure in a moving frame. Intersections, UV islands or influence regions alone do not identify an authored vamp/shaft seam. No deformation or width parameter sweep was executed.
